focus.goalkeeperReason: Agility and Reflexes carry the most weight for keepers. An FM27 training-code tester found this combined focus the best for keepers prioritising them.
focus.quicknessReason: Pace and Acceleration are among the heaviest weights in every outfield role. In harvestgreen22's test the focus took them from about +1.6 to +2.7 a season. Current Pace {pace}, Acceleration {acceleration}.
focus.attributeReason: Pace and Acceleration are already {pace} and {acceleration}, so Quickness has little left to add. {attribute} is where the {role} score has the most to gain.
focus.quicknessFallbackReason: Pace and Acceleration are among the heaviest weights in every outfield role.

trainingRole.goalkeeperReason: An FM27 training-code tester got the most growth for keepers with no role and the combined focus above.
trainingRole.outfield: {role, select, defensive {Defensive Midfielder out of possession, nothing in possession} other {Attacking Midfielder out of possession, nothing in possession}}
trainingRole.outfieldReason: An FM27 training-code tester got the strongest CA growth for young outfielders from an out-of-possession role alone, with Quickness: Defensive Midfielder for defenders, wing-backs and DMs, Attacking Midfielder for everyone else. Anticipation grew most. This comes from one tester's controlled runs.

sessions.title: Development sessions for the {role} score
sessions.note: Role-score growth from each session in harvestgreen22's FM27 test, applied to this player's attributes, as a share of the best one. "More" lists what a session builds beyond the average development session.
sessions.goalkeeper: Keepers weren't in the session test. The goalkeeping coach trains most of what a keeper needs, so assign your best one.

gapUnlikely.title: Unlikely to reach PA
gapUnlikely.detail: {gap} CA still to come at age {age}, and attributes grow little after {endAge}. Value the player closer to current ability.

minutesPeak.title: Peak development years
minutesPeak.detail: 16 to 18 is when attributes grow fastest. Minutes and the quality of the opponents both feed CA growth, so senior or loan minutes beat youth football once the player can hold a place. For the U18s, fm-scoring's author uses the minimal schedule (no tactical sessions).

minutesSenior.title: Needs senior minutes
minutesSenior.detail: Minutes played and the quality of the opponents drive how much CA a player gains. If there's no starting place for them at your club, loan them to the strongest club that will start them.

minutesPast.title: Past the development window
minutesPast.detail: Attributes grow little after {endAge}. Training from here mostly reshapes what is already there.

profHigh.title: {attribute} {value}
profHigh.detail: fm-scoring's notes point to Professionalism as the hidden attribute that matters most for growth. This level helps a player get the most out of their PA.

profLow.title: {level, select, low {Low {attribute} ({value})} other {Average {attribute} ({value})}}
profLow.detail: fm-scoring's notes point to Professionalism as the hidden attribute that matters most for growth. Mentoring is how FM changes personality: put the player in a mentoring group with senior players high in Professionalism (fm-scoring includes a mentors player search filter).

det.title: {attribute} {value}
det.detail: Training never moves Determination. Mentoring is the way to change personality. Export with the Hidden Attributes view to see Professionalism.

schedule.title: Put the development sessions on one day
schedule.detail: Only Possession, Attacking and Defensive Ball Work, Conditioning, Heavy Conditioning and Individual Development grow attributes. Every other session grew CA no more than resting, and repeating a session adds little. One tester packed the development sessions into one day to keep full Rest days, which have no training-injury checks. That cut training-injury risk from 13.8% to 4.0% with almost the same growth.

plan.source: From the FM27 training research collected in <link>fm-scoring</link>: harvestgreen22's training test, the fm-scoring author's own schedule tests, and a tester who went through FM27's training code.
plan.younger: Most of it applies to younger players.
plan.odds: Growth is random month to month, so treat this as the odds, not a promise.
